conjecture: Q569: is the Pylyavskyy-Yang hexagonal puzzle tile (arXiv:1801.07667, thm:hex-tiling / thm:hexR-tiling) a BULK R-matrix piece satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation, or a bulk piece PLUS a one-sided boundary K-matrix satisfying the reflection (Sklyanin) equation? Refines Q560, which asked only whether the hex tiles satisfy a YBE. The boundary reading was suggested by sec ss:protrude, where a trapezoidal tile is introduced and explicitly forbidden outside the left edge of the puzzle.
note:
PROVE 2026-10-23 c2. ANSWERED: NEITHER ARM. One geometric identification does all the work -- hex and hexR are the two orientation-keyed alternating labellings of the CLOSED VERTEX STAR of the triangular lattice (the union of the six unit triangles containing a lattice vertex; vertices-minus-centroid = the six unit directions, exact). Consequences, all proved: the hexagon is a bulk piece indexed by its CENTRE; it fails to fit inside a wall iff its centre LIES ON the wall, and then exactly 3 of 6 triangles are outside, so protrusion is by exactly one lattice step -- which is the content of the paper's footnote 'we require partitions to be slightly smaller'; and the ss:protrude trapezoid IS hex intersect half-plane, every retained edge label unchanged, the only new edges being the two unit edges of the length-2 cut (labels 0 above the centre, 1 below).

P2 (the risky pre-registered arm, reflection equation with trap as K) REFUTED on three independent grounds: (a) ZERO MODULI -- trap is determined by the bulk piece and the wall, whereas a K-matrix is an independent RE solution with its own spectral parameter and generically a family; (b) the KTW bulk set is CHIRAL -- no lattice reflection preserves it, because the rhombus rule ('0 clockwise of an acute angle') is handed and a reflection sends each rhombus to the complementary labelling, which is not a KTW piece; (c) sigma_W(hex) = hexR -- the hexagon is wall-reflection-invariant as a REGION but not as a LABELLED TILE, and hexR computes a different coefficient in a different ambient rectangle, so the two halves of a straddling hexagon are mirror images as shapes with mismatched labels. There is no reflection symmetry at the wall for a reflection equation to express.

P3 REFUTED AS STATED and replaced by something stronger: hex and hexR are not two one-sided boundaries of one bulk model, they are ONE tile in the two triangle-orientation conventions -- exchanged by every element of D_6 that swaps up/down triangles (odd rotations, and the three reflections whose axes lie along edge directions). thm:hexR-tiling is thm:hex-tiling conjugated by k -> n-k with transposed partitions: the paper DEFINES d~ := d^{nu'}_{la'mu'} (ktiles.tex 757-760) and the rectangle bookkeeping matches exactly ((k-1)x(n-k) transposes to k*x(n*-k*-1) with k*=n-k, n*=n). So ONE boundary phenomenon seen twice through Grassmannian duality. Additionally the one-unit shrink is NOT INTRINSIC: it is one of two equivalent bookkeeping devices for the same clipping.

P1 SPLIT: its conclusion ('not a plain YBE') stands but its reason was wrong -- the prediction quantified over 'any assignment of spectral parameters and weights' and no such object exists, since the tiles all have weight 1 and the theorems count cardinalities. The well-posed replacement is a measured negative: ten of the seventeen tiles violate LINE CONSERVATION (the 1-triangles, K, tri, hex, hexR, hex2 and trap each carry exactly one 1-edge in each of the three direction classes -- odd in all three), so the 1-edges form a branching Y-junction graph, not a conserving line model, and the tile set is not a vertex model at all. SCOPE REPORTED: this does NOT say Grassmannian puzzles are non-integrable (they are known to be, and the paper's own tri piece is Wheeler-Zinn-Justin's, obtained FROM an integrable model) -- only that the integrable structure does not live on these faces with these labels as line occupations. Whether hex has an R-matrix provenance in another presentation is OPEN and explicitly not settled. P4 CONFIRMED: the degree-inequality flip is product-vs-coproduct (|nu|>=|la|+|mu| for G_la G_mu, <= for Delta G_nu), orthogonal to the wall, i.e. the red herring P4 predicted it was.

POSITIVE CONTROLS, four of them, against an INDEPENDENT engine built from set-valued tableaux (G_la = sum_T (-1)^{|T|-|la|} x^T, multiplied/comultiplied as actual polynomials, G-basis peeled by degree triangularity -- touches no puzzle and no tableau rule from the paper). KTW count = 2 on the paper's running example; K/c 208/208 and tri/c~ 208/208 and hex/d 187/187 and hexR/d~ 54/54 at n=5,k=2; hex/d 875/875 at n=6,k=3 (the one-level-up test, moving k off 2). Boundary convention verified edge-by-edge against figure 'bdry' (27/27).

ALSO VERIFIED: the paper's UNPROVED ss:protrude claim ('Here is the complete set of tiles', no theorem, no proof). The refined 12-tile set at side n and the plain hex set at side n+1 both reproduce d: 187/187 (44 nonzero) at ambient 2x2, 875/875 (143 nonzero) at ambient 2x3. And on the paper's own ss:protrude example (la=(2,1), mu=(4,2), nu=(4,3,1), k=3) the protrusion loss is QUANTIFIED: d=4 independently, plain hex at side 7 gives 2, at side 8 gives 4, refined set at side 7 gives 4.

INSTRUMENT FAULT, the session's main one. My D_6 action implemented reflections by reversing a tile's step ORDER without negating the directions (d -> d+3). Reversing the order alone permutes a closed walk's edges into a DIFFERENT polygon -- which still closes and is still counterclockwise, so NEITHER my closure assertion NOR my signed-area assertion detected it. The wrong code said sigma_W(hex) = hex and I had already written a paragraph explaining the clipping BY that invariance; the fixed code says sigma_W(hex) = hexR, which reverses the sign of the central argument. LESSON IN THE FORM TO KEEP: two invariants that are both invariant under edge permutation cannot detect an edge permutation -- the control has to separate the orbit, here act(act(x,g),g^-1)==x (now 204/204 (tile,g) pairs) plus an independent orientation test (does g send an up-triangle to an up-triangle? -- which is also what classifies WHICH reflections swap hex and hexR). Note that the WRONG intermediate still produced the RIGHT final identity trap = hex cap H+, for the wrong reason; region-invariance and label-invariance had been merged.

SECOND INSTRUMENT NOTE, about my own citation index. The sources.json entry for 1801.07667 (upgraded to verified-quote earlier today) records 'transpose/duality symmetry d~^nu_{la,mu} = d^{nu'}_{la',mu'} holds 16/16, 0 differ' as a verification. That identity is the paper's DEFINITION of d~ (ktiles.tex 757-760), so the check was CIRCULAR -- it can only ever return 16/16. The surrounding controls in that entry (the coproduct control Delta(G_1), 1-G_1 group-like) are real; this one is not, and the entry should not be read as corroborating the duality.

GAPS, precisely: (1) the ss:protrude equivalence is COMPUTED not PROVED -- no bijection; the candidate ('clip every wall-centred hexagon; read the extra leading 0 of sigma(.,n+1,k) as a frozen strip of 0-triangles') is checked only as far as the corner triangle U(0,0) being forced to be a 0-triangle, which it is, uniquely. (2) Integrability settled only in the tested presentation. (3) The 'K-matrices generically form a family' clause of the zero-moduli argument is general knowledge, not from a source read this session; the hard half (trap determined by hex and W) is proved. (4) Census domains reach only n<=6, k<=3, ambient 2x3.

NEXT: the Gap-1 bijection looks tractable and would supply the proof the paper omits. Recorded but NOT allocated a question number (prove-session rule: no new conjectures): the vertex star is the natural face of the DUAL honeycomb lattice, which is where Grassmannian puzzle integrability usually lives -- so Theorem (vertex star) is encouraging for an R-matrix provenance for hex in the Wheeler-Zinn-Justin presentation rather than on its own faces. For the dream cycle.

tree.approach: Q569: boundary-vs-bulk for the Pylyavskyy-Yang hexagonal puzzle tiles

children.approach: all 17 tiles extracted from the e-print's own tikz edge macros into CCW edge-labelled polygons; closure and positive signed area verified for each; boundary convention verified edge-by-edge (27/27) against figure 'bdry'

Engine B: G_la from set-valued tableaux, polynomial multiplication and comultiplication, G-basis expansion by degree triangularity. Controls: min-degree part of G_la is s_la; c^nu at |nu|=|la|+|mu| reproduces classical LR for s_21^2. Touches no puzzle and no tableau rule from the paper

all four of the paper's tiling theorems reproduced against Engine B: K/c 208/208, tri/c~ 208/208, hex/d 187/187, hexR/d~ 54/54 at n=5 k=2; hex/d 875/875 at n=6 k=3. Census domain stated in the artifact, not 'small cases'

THEOREM: hex and hexR are the two orientation-keyed alternating labellings of the closed vertex star St(v). Proof: the unit triangles containing v are {v, v+D_j, v+D_{j+1}}; their outer edges concatenate to the hexagonal walk; vertices-minus-centroid = the six unit directions exactly; consecutive triangles have opposite orientation, so the two alternation classes ARE the two orientation classes

THEOREM: St(v) straddles a lattice line W iff v is ON W, and then splits 3+3 with W cap St(v) a length-2 segment. Proof: in the basis where W={a=0} and e_1 lies along W, the six neighbours have a-coordinates a_v+(1,0,-1,-1,0,1), so St(v) occupies a_v-1<=a<=a_v+1 with both extremes attained. Explains the paper's 'slightly smaller' footnote

THEOREM: trap = hex intersect {a>=0} as labelled tiles -- 3 of 6 triangles retained, all retained edge labels unchanged, the only new boundary edges the two unit edges of the length-2 cut (0 above the centre, 1 below). Verified exactly on covered triangles and on labelled boundary edges

PROPOSITION: no lattice reflection preserves the KTW tile set. The rhombus rule ('0 clockwise of an acute angle') is handed; a reflection reverses handedness and sends each rhombus to the complementary labelling, which is not a KTW piece. Verified for all six reflections (rotations all preserve the set)

PROPOSITION: sigma_W(hex) = hexR. The wall is a lattice line so sigma_W has its axis along an edge direction, hence exchanges triangle orientations, hence exchanges the two orientation-keyed labellings. Regionally sigma_W fixes St(v). This is the sharpest of the three anti-reflection grounds: under the wall reflection the hexagon returns as a DIFFERENT tile computing a DIFFERENT coefficient

PROPOSITION: in the ss:protrude set a 1-edge in the wall's direction class carries label 1 iff it lies on the wall and 2 iff interior. Proof from CCW orientation (interior on the left, so direction-1 edges are a tile's lower-right side and direction-4 its upper-left) plus the paper's relabel-and-duplicate rule. No sum over boundary states: the label is a deterministic function of wall-adjacency, not an amplitude

PROPOSITION (well-posed replacement for the ill-posed P1): ten of the seventeen tiles violate line conservation, each carrying exactly one 1-edge in each of the three direction classes. So the 1-edges branch at Y-junctions rather than conserving, and the tiles are not vertices of a line model. Scope explicitly limited: says nothing about other presentations, and does not claim puzzles are non-integrable

CORROBORATION, explicitly NOT a premise -- the root's answer to Q569 does not depend on it, and it is carried at 'computed' rather than inflated. Test of the paper's UNPROVED ss:protrude claim ('Here is the complete set of tiles', no theorem, no proof): refined 12-tile set at side n = plain hex at side n+1 = d. Verified 187/187 (44 nonzero) at ambient 2x2 and 875/875 (143 nonzero) at ambient 2x3, plus the paper's own example (d=4; side-7 plain hex 2; side-8 plain hex 4; side-7 refined 4), which quantifies the protrusion loss as exactly 2 tilings. The only downstream statement that leans on it is the corollary 'the one-unit shrink is not intrinsic', which the artifact also marks computed and lists as Gap 1; the P3 refutation rests instead on the proved duality node. No bijection.
